payload.text:
The safety floors hold in compiler and runtime, and ?speed= cannot cross them. hv RULED 2026-09-09: max_ease is capped at 2400. That is ONE constant and it closes the whole crossing space STRUCTURALLY rather than by refusal -- runtime ease <= 2400 < 2500 <= runtime dwell, for every config, every speed and both pace modes. vc verified the envelope in source before putting it up: cc was right that no compile-time enforcement closes it, because at ?speed=16 a config with dwell 20000 and ease 2600 crosses while authored ease sits eight times under authored dwell, so the compiler cannot see it. What the measurement added is that BOTH defects -- the constants crossing at speed=1, and the dwellOf/easeOf asymmetry crossing at any speed -- reduce to one condition, runtime ease exceeding the 2500 dwell floor. Capping below that floor makes it unreachable rather than refused, which is the difference between a guard and a rule. Cost: no reel may crossfade slower than 2.4s; 45h's worst authored ease is 900, so nothing real moves. Raising min_dwell instead would also work and was not taken, because it changes pacing for every existing slide.

THE RUNTIME LEG'S MECHANISM, SPECIFIED 2026-09-09 18:55Z BEFORE cc PULLS THE TEMPLATE, BECAUSE AFTER IT LANDS THE SAME SENTENCE IS A REVIEW COMMENT. Measured at the reference: `player.html:561` is `const LIM = REEL.limits`, so the cap is READ OFF THE PAYLOAD and is not a JS literal -- the player's own comment gives the reason, "a safety limit that exists twice, in two languages, is one limit and one liability." THE LEG THEREFORE REDUCES TO TWO SOURCE CHECKS AND NEEDS NO PIXEL: the emitted payload's `limits.max_ease` DERIVES from `limits::MAX_EASE_MS`, and the pulled template still reads `LIM = REEL.limits`. Red-control that can fire: flip `MAX_EASE_MS` to 3000, rebuild, and the payload must follow; if it still reads 2400 there is a second home, which is the one-limit-two-homes defect this module was written to fix, re-created by the commit that ports the fix.
THE NEGATIVE HALF IS CITED AS TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS RATHER THAN AS A HARNESS ROW, AND THAT IS snorkeltoast'S CORRECTION OF vc, VERIFIED AT SOURCE BEFORE BEING TAKEN. (i) `signature()` at `showreel-harness:232` walks `payload.get("slides", [])` only, so NO top-level block -- `limits` included -- is structural to that instrument. (ii) the capture URL at `showreel-harness:1098` is `?start={index}&noloop&kiosk&nobug`, carrying no `pace=`, with a boxed comment above it recording that `&pace=ambient` was there and was the single worst defect in that harness. Both stay true whatever `max_ease` says on either side.
WHY NOT THE ROW, AND vc WOULD HAVE BEEN THE PROXIMATE CAUSE OF ITS OWN DANGLING CITATION. vc first cited snorkeltoast's `shipped-max-ease` expectation, kind BLIND. `_shipped_max_ease` returns `[]` the moment `compiler.LIMITS["max_ease"] == PORT_MAX_EASE_MS` -- its docstring says it "retires itself the day the Python side is capped" -- and capping Python is hv item 2, WHICH vc IS CARRYING TO hv. So the citation was contingent on a defect vc is asking hv to fix. **Cite the durable fact, not the contingent conclusion resting on it**; that is "cite the token, not the line" one level up, where what expires is not a line number but the finding.
NO AMBIENT CAPTURE ARM, AND THE EXPERIMENT IS ALREADY ON DISK. `showreel-harness:1088-1092` records it: slide 3, budgets 1100 vs 4520 -- with `pace=ambient` RMSE 142.827361, without it 0.000000, and with `pace=ambient` at 1400 (past the SCALED ease) 0.000000. The 142.8 was a capture-WINDOW artefact, budgets computed `ease + 200` from the payload's 900 while the runtime ran 1260, and NOT a `max_ease` divergence. So an arm on 45h has two possible outcomes and both are measured. The independent leg agrees: 900 x 1.4 = 1260, which is 1140ms short of the cap.
AND THE TWO CROSSING NUMBERS ARE TWO PREDICATES, RECORDED AS A PAIR SO THEY STOP LOOKING LIKE ONE NUMBER MEASURED TWICE. Divergence from the cap needs authored ease x 1.4 > 2400, so above 1714.29 -- 1715ms, vc's. Ease reaching the dwell floor needs 2500 / 1.4, so above 1785.71 -- 1786ms, snorkeltoast's, and it is `_ease_meets_dwell`'s predicate rather than this one. Both correct, neither superseding the other. A two-number discrepancy on one subject is exactly what gets filed as explained and never looked up.
THE PAYLOAD MUST CARRY A TOP-LEVEL `limits` BLOCK, THE PLAYER DOES NOT DEFEND ITSELF, AND THE HARNESS CANNOT SEE THE OMISSION. Found by snorkeltoast 2026-09-10 07:11Z while reading the PUBLISHED artifact, verified by vc at source in both players, and recorded here an hour before cc emits a first payload.
THE PLAYER HAS NO FALLBACK. `const LIM = REEL.limits` -- `player.html:562` in this tree, `:775` in artifact 009 -- and `LIM.min_dwell`, `LIM.min_ease` and `LIM.max_ease` are read straight off it. A payload with no `limits` key leaves `LIM` undefined and THROWS ON THE FIRST SLIDE: the reel does not run at all. The OLD published player survived a limits-less payload because its floors were inline literals (`published.html:709` and `:712`, hardcoded 2500 / 600 / 3000); the current one cannot, and that is not a regression -- it is the direct consequence of this row's template half, which exists so the cap is READ OFF THE PAYLOAD rather than restated in JavaScript.
AND THE HARNESS IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO IT, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS A ROW AND NOT A NOTE. `signature(payload)` walks `payload.get("slides", [])` and nothing else, so TOP-LEVEL payload keys are never compared. **A port that emits every slide correctly and omits `limits` PASSES THE STRUCTURE COMPARISON CLEAN**, then fails on pixels as a total blank with no diagnosis -- the instrument pointing at the slides while the fault is a key that is not there. **So this row's runtime leg cannot lean on the harness's structure comparison, because that comparison cannot see the block the row is about.**
snorkeltoast IS ADDING A TOP-LEVEL PAYLOAD-KEY CHECK that refuses with the missing key NAMED rather than discovering it in pixels, held until the running control lands. cc has been told not to wait for it and to emit the key.
AND A MEASUREMENT THAT SEPARATES THIS ROW FROM hv's ITEM 2 RATHER THAN MERGING THEM: the published artifact applies the SAME THREE VALUES this row is about, inline -- 2500, 600, 3000 -- so the 3000-against-2500 crossing ALREADY EXISTS in the live reel at the same magnitudes. Promoting a rebuilt artifact to the published slot is SAFETY-NEUTRAL: it neither creates nor fixes the crossing, and only the mechanism moves from inline constants to a payload the player reads. hv item 2 stays a standalone ruling.
THE CLAUSE ABOVE SAYS "THE PAYLOAD MUST CARRY A TOP-LEVEL `limits` BLOCK" AND THAT RULE WOULD REFUSE A SOUND ARTIFACT. Corrected 2026-09-10 07:58Z by snorkeltoast, who found it while BUILDING the check vc had described -- and who asked vc to correct the row rather than forward the first version. **The currently-published 45h build carries no `limits` key anywhere, embeds the OLD player, applies 2500 / 600 / 3000 inline at its `:709` and `:712`, and is entirely correct.** A blanket required-key rule condemns it. **A false refusal from the instrument is worse than the blind spot it replaces, because the blind at least fails only on the guilty.**
**THE INVARIANT IS INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, NOT A REQUIRED KEY: an artifact whose OWN EMBEDDED PLAYER reads `REEL.limits` unguarded must carry the keys that player reads.** Both halves ship in the same file, so it is answerable from the artifact ALONE -- no policy, no version table, and no standing agreement between implementations about which player is current. **The check follows the player rather than a rule anybody agreed once**, which is why it stays true after the player changes.
PROVED DIFFERENTIALLY, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT MEAN ANYTHING: two artifacts that BOTH lack `limits`, told apart by what their own player does -- the published build PROCEEDS, and a copy of 009 with the key stripped is REFUSED with the key named. Either one alone would have been consistent with a rule that is simply wrong. Landed at `75a5ea2`, eight pure selftest cases.
**SO WHAT THIS ROW ASKS OF THE PORT IS NARROWER THAN vc FIRST WROTE, AND cc HAS BOTH VERSIONS.** The port does NOT owe `limits` as a matter of policy. It owes `limits` **IF it substitutes into the current `player.html`**, because that shell does `const LIM = REEL.limits` at `:562` with no fallback and reads `min_dwell`, `min_ease` and `max_ease` off it at `:562-564`. cc is substituting into exactly that shell, so the obligation binds today -- and **if cc ever ships a player with a GUARDED read, the requirement lifts by itself and the harness stops asking.**
AND A THIRD INSTANCE OF A FAMILY THIS CONTRACT NOW HAS THREE OF: snorkeltoast wrote the player text in those selftest cases out LITERALLY rather than building it from the `LIM_UNGUARDED_RE` under test. **A fixture derived from the pattern it tests agrees with it by construction and follows a rename silently while staying green** -- the same reason their `__PRODUCER__` cases assert the literal token, and the same defect as cc's `embed=` assertion that read the constant on both sides. Vacuous, and dressed as rigour.
